title: GDExtension: Duplicate keys in .gdextension overwrite in non-intuitive order
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in 4.6
Reproducible on `master` at time of writing

### System information

Godot v4.6.1.stable (f1c733f9b) - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 3 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9636) - AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D 16-Core Processor (32 threads) - 93.64 GiB memory

### Issue description

If a `.gdextension` file contains duplicate keys in the `libraries` section, it will unintuitively use the _last_ value provided for that key in the file. This can cause unexpected behavior since library loading uses a "first most-specific" pattern to select libraries, but duplicate keys can cause a discrepancy between order of matching and the value associated.

With examples:
```
[libraries]

windows.editor = "./mylib1.dll"
windows.editor.x86_64 = "./mylib2.dll"
windows.debug.x86_64 = "./mylib3.dll"
```

In this case, `mylib2` will be selected -- the first line matches, but it will be superseded by the second line because it matches more tags. The third line also matches but will be skipped because it doesn't have _more_ tags than the second line (see `gdextension_library_loader.cpp:93`). This seems like desirable behavior.

```
[libraries]

windows.editor = "./mylib1.dll"
windows.editor.x86_64 = "./mylib2.dll"
windows.debug.x86_64 = "./mylib3.dll"
windows.editor.x86_64 = "./mylib4.dll"
```

In this case, `mylib4` will be selected. When parsing, `config_file.cpp._parse()` will overwrite the stored value for key `windows.editor.x86_64` to `mylib4`, but its order of evaluation is unchanged. The key `windows.editor.x86_64` will still be the first most-specific key but its value was updated to `mylib4`. 

This is obviously a severe edge case, but easy to run into with some mistakes in configuration. I ran into this as I am building a GDExtension library that can run in multiple modes on the same platform (e.g. "standard" and "portable mode"). I have separate binaries for each, and separate export presets to tag each. I want to include an option to override the default option when playing out of the editor. You can't assign custom tags when playing in the editor, so instead I just leave a comment in the `.gdextension` that just says "Uncomment this line to switch to enable portable mode in editor". Paradoxically, I have to put that line at the _bottom_ of the file instead of the top, even though libraries are matched top to bottom.

A fix is easy here -- check for duplicate keys when parsing `.gdextension` and don't overwrite existing values. If this is actually the desired behavior, then GDExtension library loading should match "last most-specific" instead of first (and I can update the connected PR).

### Steps to reproduce

Create any GDExtension with multiple libraries that could target the same platform and provide duplicate keys in the `libraries` section of the `.gdextension` file.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A, just requires any GDExtension plugin that ships multiple different binaries for the same platform
